title: Co-Creating Patient Partnerships Within a National Cancer Clinical Trials Network
content: Structured patient partnership is increasingly recognised in oncology research, yet how trial groups and charities can collaborate to sustain it system-wide is less well described. Cancer Trials Ireland (CTI) established a patient partnership model supported by the Irish Cancer Society (ICS). This paper reviews the model’s development since its inception, aligned with the International Association for Public Participation’s (IAP2) Spectrum of Public Participation. The review draws on institutional records, co-author recollection, organisational learnings, barriers and facilitators, research and strategic outputs, and national and international collaborations. By 2026, 33 patient partners were embedded across all adult disease-specific sub-groups (DSSGs), with patient representation on CTI governance. Facilitators included a funded coordination role, enhanced recruitment, aligned messaging, structural scaffolding, and shared advocacy; barriers included patient diversity, competing commitments, perceptions, and sustainable funding. Patient partners have contributed to investigator-initiated trial concepts and grant applications, and to policy activity, including the National Clinical Trials Oversight Group, the Climate Change Charter, data protection legislation, government general election manifesto advocacy, and public campaigns. Patient-initiated, designed, and led research projects have resulted in international presentations and publications. A structured trials partnership can accelerate and sustain patient partnership beyond individual studies, embedding patient perspectives across trial selection, development, and dissemination, and in shaping policy.
